prose: CNBC reports OpenAI will bring its models to Google Cloud's model garden and the Antigravity coding tool in the coming weeks, completing its presence on all three top clouds after the AWS launch in April, which followed Microsoft losing its exclusive license on OpenAI's IP less than six months ago. The move is about enterprise distribution as OpenAI builds beyond its consumer roots and courts investors at a $1.4 trillion valuation ahead of a targeted IPO. Google's cloud, meanwhile, is on a run: annualized growth accelerated to about 82% in Q2 from 63% in Q1, versus 37% for Amazon and 42% for Microsoft, with all three reporting next week. Ramp data shows most business AI spending still goes to OpenAI and Anthropic.
highlights: OpenAI models coming to Google Cloud model garden and Antigravity in weeks
Completes presence on all three major clouds; AWS launch was in April
Follows Microsoft losing exclusive IP license less than six months ago
OpenAI courting investors at a $1.4T valuation, IPO targeted
Google Cloud growth accelerated to ~82% annualized in Q2 vs 37% AWS, 42% Microsoft
All three hyperscalers report earnings next week
